prompt:
(a) Explain how the continuous random collisions of gas molecules with the walls of a container produce a steady pressure. [2]
(b) A fixed mass of an ideal gas is held at constant volume. State and explain what happens to the gas pressure if the mean-square speed <c^2> of the molecules is doubled. [2]

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) Explains that molecules undergo changes in momentum when they collide with the walls, exerting normal forces on the walls by Newton's second and third laws.
(a) Explains that the very large number of frequent random collisions distributed uniformly over the wall area produces a steady average macroscopic force per unit area (pressure = F / A).
(b) States that the pressure is doubled (increases by a factor of 2).

(b) Explains using pV = (1/3) N m <c^2>: since V, N, and m are constant, pressure p is directly proportional to <c^2> (or: molecules deliver greater momentum change per collision AND collide more frequently).

hints: In (a), structure the explanation around momentum change, force, collision frequency, and force per unit area.
In (b), cite the kinetic theory pressure equation pV = (1/3) N m <c^2> and identify which terms are held constant.
solution:
(a) When gas molecules collide with the container walls, their velocity changes direction, producing a change in momentum. By Newton's second and third laws, each collision exerts a normal force on the wall. Because there is a vast number of molecules moving randomly and colliding at an extremely high frequency across the entire inner surface, these individual microscopic impacts smooth out into a steady, uniform average force per unit area, which constitutes the gas pressure.
(b) The pressure doubles. From the kinetic theory equation pV = (1/3) N m <c^2>, for a fixed mass of gas (constant N and m) in a rigid container (constant V), pressure p is directly proportional to mean-square speed <c^2>. Therefore, doubling <c^2> doubles the pressure.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Look for two key stages: (1) momentum change produces force on wall; (2) large number of frequent collisions gives steady force per unit area.
Part (b): State clearly that pressure doubles, and justify using p proportional to <c^2> when V and mass are constant.
